claim: Real enforcement lives at the database engine level, not in prompting alone; database roles for exploratory tools must have SELECT privileges only with no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE
quote: Prompting tells the model what you want, not what it's allowed to do. Real security enforcement must occur at the database layer itself, not through LLM instructions.

claim: OWASP identifies giving an AI agent a database role with write permissions when only read access is needed as a core excessive-agency vulnerability
quote: Giving an AI agent an IAM role or an API key, and the agent using it in an unintended way. Example: a Lambda function with database write permissions when only read access was needed.

claim: OWASP LLM06:2025 Excessive Agency recommends deploying multiple agents with least-privilege configurations instead of one powerful agent with broad access
quote: Rather than deploying one powerful agent with broad access, multiple agents with least-privilege configurations ensure each agent accesses only the specific resources required.

claim: PostgreSQL 14+ provides the pg_read_all_data predefined role granting SELECT on all tables and USAGE on all schemas, but it does not bypass RLS policies
quote: Care should be taken when granting these roles to ensure they are only used where needed and with the understanding that these roles grant access to privileged information.

claim: The recommended modern approach for PostgreSQL read-only users is GRANT pg_read_all_data TO role, which covers objects created by any user including future ones
quote: GRANT pg_read_all_data TO scraper; This approach lets you assign the read only privileges to a user; the user is able to have read only privileges on any objects created by any user in the database.

claim: PGOPTIONS='-c default_transaction_read_only=on' sets session-level read-only mode but is a safety convenience, not a security boundary, since any user can revoke it
quote: True protection requires a special-purpose read-only user when connecting from untrusted tools or applications.

claim: The default_transaction_read_only parameter can be overridden in a session even when set database-wide, making role-level GRANTs the only true security enforcement
quote: default_transaction_read_only can be overridden in a session, even if the value is set database-wide. A user can execute SET default_transaction_read_only TO off to bypass protections and perform writes.

claim: SQL Server least-privilege role pattern uses CREATE ROLE with schema-scoped GRANT SELECT, avoiding db_owner and public role inheritance
quote: Every login, user, and role should have only the permissions required to perform its job. Avoid inheriting permissions through db_owner or public roles.

claim: MySQL read-only user is created with GRANT SELECT ON database.* and should use a specific host instead of % in production
quote: Restrict host access: use a specific host instead of % in production to limit connection origins. Avoid global SELECT: granting SELECT ON *.* exposes system schemas unnecessarily.

claim: SQLite read-only mode is enforced via URI connection string with mode=readonly parameter; any write attempt raises OperationalError
quote: By appending ?mode=readonly to the database's file path and setting the uri parameter of connect to True, we instruct sqlite3 to open the database without write permissions.

claim: SQLite's set_authorizer callback is the official mechanism for compile-time SQL restriction; it can deny INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DROP while permitting SELECT at the statement compilation level
quote: An authorizer is used when preparing SQL statements from an untrusted source, to ensure that the SQL statements do not try to access data they are not allowed to see, or that they do not try to execute malicious statements that damage the database.

claim: Python's sqlite3 set_authorizer can enforce read-only operation by returning SQLITE_OK only for SQLITE_SELECT actions and SQLITE_DENY for all others
quote: The callback checks the action type and only allows SELECT statements. All other operations are denied by returning SQLITE_DENY, which raises a DatabaseError.

claim: PostgreSQL column-level GRANT restricts SELECT to named columns; a table-level SELECT grant overrides column restrictions, so revoke table access first
quote: Column access to particular columns will not work if users already have SELECT access on the whole table.

claim: RLS filters which rows are visible while column masking controls how much detail is shown; combined they provide two-dimensional data access control
quote: Row-Level Security determines who sees what records, while masking controls how much detail they see.

claim: The most robust security combines RLS with column masking, creating layered protection against application bugs or unauthorized LLM query access
quote: RLS filters which rows users access while column masking hides sensitive columns within those rows, creating layered protection against application bugs or unauthorized query access.

claim: SQLAlchemy's postgresql_readonly=True execution option issues SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY at the connection level, adding a session-layer guard on top of role-level grants
quote: For PostgreSQL, most dialects support setting the READ ONLY characteristic of transactions by passing the postgresql_readonly flag with Connection.execution_options().

claim: pgBouncer routes reads to standby (read-only) servers and writes to the primary by mapping virtual database names, providing infrastructure-level enforcement
quote: PgBouncer acts as a proxy, mapping virtual database names to backend servers. The reads pool directs through HAProxy, which load-balances across multiple standby nodes.

claim: A read replica is the strongest physical boundary for AI/LLM SQL agents because DROP, DELETE, and UPDATE commands are structurally impossible regardless of injection
quote: Read-only replicas serve as a physical boundary for AI agents, creating a logical and physical impossibility for DROP, DELETE, or UPDATE commands to succeed, no matter how clever an injection.

claim: Stored procedures invert the security model: instead of blocking what the LLM cannot do, it can only call approved procedures with enumerated parameters
quote: Instead of telling the LLM what it can't do, you only let it choose from what it can do. Anything outside of this whitelist is simply not possible.

claim: Best practices for LLM-to-SQL connections include read-only credentials, column restrictions at the schema layer, query LIMIT enforcement, and EXPLAIN-based cost gates
quote: Only SELECT allowed. No INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE, no DDL. Add timeouts and a dry-run mode that returns EXPLAIN PLAN before execution for high-cost queries.

claim: Effective least privilege for AI spans identity/PAM, policy engine, database enforcement, and monitoring layers; application-only controls fail when agents talk directly to the DB
quote: Application-only controls fail when agents talk directly to the DB or multiple tools access shared data. The database must enforce boundaries regardless of which agent initiates the query.

claim: Only 37-40% of organizations have actual containment controls despite 58-59% monitoring AI agents; read-only defaults and purpose-specific service accounts are key mitigations
quote: Many agents require only read access; write permissions demand explicit justification. Agents receive permissions aligned solely to their intended function with automatic expiration.

claim: PostgreSQL's default_transaction_read_only parameter can be set per-role via ALTER ROLE but cannot be treated as a security boundary because any user can override it
quote: Breaking out of this restriction is no harder than issuing SET default_transaction_read_only = off. That ALTER ROLE might protect against accidental changes, but it's certainly no form of security restriction.

claim: RLS moves filtering enforcement into the database itself so every query is filtered automatically, including those written by users and LLMs
quote: Embedded dashboards run too many queries—including ones written by users and LLMs—for application-level filtering to be safe, so Row-Level Security pushes the rules into the database where every query is filtered automatically.

claim: OWASP LLM06:2025 identifies three root causes of excessive agency: excessive functionality, excessive permissions, and excessive autonomy; mitigation requires granular role-specific permissions
quote: Excessive Agency occurs when an LLM is granted too much functionality, permissions, or autonomy, enabling it to perform unintended or harmful actions. Assign minimal and role-specific permissions to LLM extensions interacting with other systems.
